official.deadline_note: The 2027/2028 Foreign Development Cooperation call ran 1 August - 30 September 2026 (MEYS wording: 'from 21 August until 30 September 2026') and is closed as of 2026-10-10. No separate institutional deadline is published by the Faculty; the Czech Embassy sets its own deadline for the interview and for uploading the required documents after the initial evaluation, and applicants already enrolled at a Czech university had to mail a printed, personally signed application to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs by 20 December 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle of the Foreign Development Cooperation programme (call 01.08.2026-30.09.2026; studies begin in the academic year 2027/2028)
official.status_note: MEYS states the applications period for the academic year 2027/2028 ran until 30 September 2026, and the DZS Study in Czechia portal shows the 2027/2028 English-language call as 01.08.2026-30.09.2026 with 'currently no open calls for this activity'. Evaluation of applications runs 1 October - 31 January, selected applicants are contacted by the Embassy for an interview, final proposals are forwarded to the Czech Republic in January 2027 and the decision is delivered through the respective Embassy by the end of June 2027 (MEYS FAQ reports selected applicants are informed in June/July).
official.tuition_coverage_note: DZS portal (awarding body's implementing agency): 'Tuition fees are paid on behalf of the scholarship holders by the Government of the Czech Republic.' Faculty of Social Sciences UK: the scholarship 'fully covers tuition fees of selected Master's study programs'.
benefits: Tuition fees of the selected study programme are paid on behalf of the scholarship holder by the Government of the Czech Republic

Monthly scholarship of CZK 16,000 for a follow-up Master's study programme (CZK 24,960 for a Doctoral programme), intended to cover the necessary costs related to staying and studying in the Czech Republic
Option of accommodation in student dormitories and meals in student canteens, paid from the scholarship under the same conditions as for citizens of the Czech Republic
Subsidy towards health insurance / health services provided by the Ministry of Health to the same extent as for Czech insured persons
Scholarship granted for the standard duration of full-time study in the chosen programme
eligibility: Citizens of 13 listed countries only for the 2027/2028 cycle: Bangladesh, Belarus (democratic opposition), Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Gabon, Georgia, Guatemala, Honduras, Mauritania, Palestine, Ukraine, Zambia
Neither a citizen of the Czech Republic, nor a citizen of the European Union, nor any other foreign national with a permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic may apply
Permanent residence in an eligible country is not enough - citizenship of a listed country is required
Follow-up Master's applicants must have completed a bachelor's study programme; graduates of a Master's programme can no longer be awarded a scholarship at the same or a lower level

Only applicants who are not enrolled at a university in the Czech Republic at the time of application are eligible for this particular call (a separate call exists for students already studying in Czechia)
The DZS portal lists an age window for this call: date of birth after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008
requirements: Electronic application form submitted through the official Study in Czechia register by 30 September 2026, complete only after the motivation letter and the mandatory tests are submitted
Mandatory online entrance English language test taken during the application submission, proving sufficient command of English
Mandatory General academic aptitude (General Study Prerequisites) test
Each applicant may register only once and submit only one application; incomplete applications with missing mandatory attachments are not accepted for further consideration
Motivation letter of one A4 page emphasising the practical application of the learning and the benefit to the applicant's country of origin after graduation
Academic CV focused on studies and employment

Faculty of Social Sciences UK additionally publishes for its English-taught Master's programmes (e.g. International Relations) IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 or above in each component, TOEFL iBT 83, Cambridge B2 First 175, Cambridge C1/C2, PTE Academic above 56, LanguageCert or Duolingo 120 - waived with at least two years of secondary-level or one year of full-degree university study conducted in English
documents: Motivation letter (one A4 page for Master's, two A4 pages for Doctoral applicants)
Application form for a scholarship of the Government of the Czech Republic (personally signed)
CV focused on studies and employment
Declaration of acceptance of the conditions for providing scholarships of the Government of the Czech Republic, signed by hand
Declaration of acceptance of the conditions for the provision of health services, signed by hand
Statutory declaration of return to the country of origin after completion of studies, signed by hand
Officially verified (apostille or superlegalised) copy of the birth certificate with a certified translation into Czech
Medical confirmation about the applicant's health no more than two months old, with certified translation into English or Czech

Officially certified copy of the foreign diploma or equivalent proof of completed bachelor's study, with a diploma supplement, with higher-level authentication (apostille/superlegalisation) and a certified translation into Czech by a sworn translator
List of completed subjects and examinations with scope and grades, with certified translation into Czech (applicants with an incomplete Bachelor's degree)
Additional information that the completed study programme was provided by an institution entitled to provide higher education, and information about the content of foreign university education
selection_criteria: Completeness first: applications missing any mandatory attachment are not accepted for further consideration
The application is evaluated only after the motivation letter and both compulsory tests (English language test and General academic aptitude test) are completed
The first part of evaluation is conducted from 1 October to 31 January; the responsible Czech Embassy then invites selected applicants to an interview and sets the document deadline
The motivation letter is assessed on the practical application of the learning and the benefit to the applicant's country of origin after graduation
Applicants already enrolled at a Czech university are assessed only after applications from abroad have been considered
There is no legal claim to the award of a scholarship
coverage: Necessary costs related to staying and studying in the Czech Republic (awarding body's own framing of the monthly scholarship)
Tuition fees of the selected study programme, paid by the Government of the Czech Republic

Accommodation in student dormitories, meals in student canteens and public transport, covered by the scholarship holder from the scholarship under the same conditions that apply to students who are citizens of the Czech Republic
Health services provided by the Ministry of Health to the same extent as for Czech insured persons; the holder pays standard regulatory fees and co-payments like a Czech insured person
application_method: Register an account on the official Study in Czechia application register (studyin.gov.cz, portal stipendia.studujnavs.gov.cz) and complete the electronic application form for the Foreign Development Cooperation - English language call

Complete both compulsory tests inside the application: the English language test and the General academic aptitude test (tests can be taken at any time up to the deadline, even in a later login session)

Upload the mandatory attachments in the personal account in the study register; after the initial evaluation, attend the Czech Embassy interview and submit the requested documents, with a printed and personally signed application and proof of the highest completed education in paper form if the Embassy so instructs
official.application_route: Apply online only - register on the official Study in Czechia portal and submit the electronic application (motivation letter, documents, English test and General academic aptitude test); the Faculty of Social Sciences does not administer the scholarship and only becomes involved after the Ministry of Education's initial selection is complete.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of one of the 13 listed countries is required; citizens of the Czech Republic, EU citizens and foreign nationals holding a permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic are excluded, and permanent residence in an eligible country does not qualify.
official.international_eligibility: International students only: the award is restricted to citizens of the 13 listed developing and specific third countries (Bangladesh, Belarus (democratic opposition), Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Gabon, Georgia, Guatemala, Honduras, Mauritania, Palestine, Ukraine, Zambia for the 2027/2028 cycle).
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The study must be taken from the MEYS list of selected follow-up Master's programmes offered in English; at the Faculty of Social Sciences, Charles University these are Economics and Finance (MEF), Finance and Data Analytics (MFDA), Geopolitical Studies (GPS), International Economic and Political Studies (IEPS), International Relations (MAIN) and International Security Studies (MISS). Once granted, neither the university nor the study programme and/or language of study may be changed.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal or dissertation outline is required for Master's applicants (a one A4 page motivation letter is required instead).
official.duration: Standard duration of full-time study - two-year follow-up Master's degree programme
official.description: The Government of the Czech Republic grants these scholarships under Resolution No. 870 as of 27 November 2024, as part of the joint foreign development cooperation programme of the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, implemented in cooperation with the Ministry of Health, so that foreign nationals from listed developing countries can study selected follow-up Master's or Doctoral programmes at Czech public universities. At the Faculty of Social Sciences, Charles University the award is offered for six English-taught two-year Master's programmes and pays the tuition fees, provides a monthly living-cost scholarship, dormitory/canteen access on Czech-student conditions and health care through the Ministry of Health.
official.program_type: Czech Government Scholarship - Developing Countries (Government of the Czech Republic Foreign Development Cooperation programme), English-language follow-up Master's study hosted by the Faculty of Social Sciences, Charles University
official.english_requirement: MEYS: an applicant for a scholarship in support of English-medium studies must sit an online entrance English language test during the application submission, which proves sufficient command of English; the application is only complete once this test and the General academic aptitude test are passed. The host faculty separately publishes certificate thresholds for its English-taught Master's programmes (e.g. IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each component, TOEFL iBT 83, Cambridge B2 First 175, PTE Academic above 56, Duolingo 120), waived after at least two years of secondary-level or one year of full-degree university study in English.

not_confirmed: No published selection rubric, scoring weights or pass marks for the English language test and General academic aptitude test
Dormitory and canteen prices (the amount of the stipend left after accommodation and food) are not published on the awarding body's pages
No 2028/2029 cycle dates have been published yet - MEYS only records that the deadline falls in September a year in advance
Programme-specific tuition fee levels at the Faculty of Social Sciences are published per programme, not per scholarship; the fee itself is waived for holders
verification.notes: Amount, tuition waiver, dormitory/canteen arrangement, health care and non-reimbursement of travel were taken from the DZS Study in Czechia call page and the MEYS binding Guidelines (both official); deadline, country list, eligible programmes and the tuition-waiver wording were cross-checked on the MEYS page and the Faculty of Social Sciences notice.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a Czech government award for citizens of 13 named countries who are not already studying at a Czech university, covering tuition plus CZK 16,000 per month for living costs - so the money to plan around is the stipend, not the fee. The 2027/2028 application window (1 August - 30 September 2026) is already closed, which means the realistic target is the next cycle opening around August 2027 for studies starting in autumn 2028. Because selection runs from a central ministry list of programmes, the single most valuable preparation step is confirming that your target programme appears on the current MEYS English-language list - the six Faculty of Social Sciences programmes (MEF, MFDA, GPS, IEPS, MAIN, MISS) all appeared in the 2026 list, but the list is refreshed annually. Note that apostilles, legalised birth certificates and Czech-translated documents take weeks to obtain, so start the paperwork in spring, not in August.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Gabon, Georgia, Guatemala, Honduras, Mauritania, Palestine, Ukraine or Zambia with a completed Bachelor's degree who want a tuition-free, English-taught two-year Master's in economics, finance, geopolitics or international relations in Prague and can fund their own flight.
application_readiness_checklist: Check your passport nationality against the 13-country list for the current cycle - residence alone does not count, and the list is reissued each year

Start the apostille/superlegalisation of your diploma and birth certificate early; a non-Hague country needs superlegalisation through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs plus the Czech Embassy, which can take several weeks
Commission certified Czech translations of the diploma, transcript and birth certificate from a sworn translator registered in the Czech list of experts
Get a medical confirmation of your health status issued within two months of submission, and have it certified
Draft the motivation letter as one A4 page that ties the degree to a concrete benefit for your home country - that framing is explicitly what MEYS asks for
Confirm your birth date falls inside the announced window (for the 2027/2028 call: after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008)
Prepare for the English and general aptitude tests before you open the portal, then complete both in one sitting before the September deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a programme that dropped off the current MEYS English-language list - the eligible programme list is reissued every academic year and cannot be checked in advance from the Faculty's own pages

Submitting an application with one missing mandatory annex (birth certificate, medical certificate, diploma supplement or content-of-education statement): incomplete applications are excluded from consideration outright
Never completing the two compulsory tests - the application is only forwarded for evaluation after the English test and the General academic aptitude test are both finished

Being caught by the citizenship rule in reverse - EU citizens, Czech citizens and permanent residents of the Czech Republic are barred, and residency in an eligible country is not a substitute for citizenship
Applying twice or registering twice: only one registration and one application per applicant is allowed, and duplicate accounts invalidate the file

Losing the award after selection by failing to arrive within 30 days of the start date in the Decision, or by exceeding the standard period of study, which terminates both scholarship and accommodation booking
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights to and from the Czech Republic are paid by the student (MEYS explicitly does not reimburse travel); MEYS advises bringing CZK 5,000-8,000 of your own money for arrival administrative fees, transport and settling in; the holder also pays Czech-style health co-payments and regulatory fees, and any care beyond the standard Ministry of Health package, at their own cost. Self-funding peers at the same faculty pay around EUR 7,000 per year in tuition (MAIN, published figure), which is what the waiver is worth.
document_audit: The birth certificate needs official verification (apostille or superlegalisation) plus a Czech translation - many applicants wrongly assume an English translation suffices

The diploma must be accompanied by a diploma supplement AND translated by a sworn translator entered in the Czech list of experts and interpreters; a translation by a non-registered translator is a classic rejection trigger
The medical certificate must be issued no more than two months before submission and, if not in English or Czech, translated - an older certificate is invalid
The motivation letter is one A4 page only for Master's applicants and must be framed around practical application and benefit to the country of origin, not personal ambition
The three declarations (scholarship terms, health services, return to the country of origin) must be signed by the applicant's own hand - typed or unsigned scans are not accepted
Only a printed, personally signed application and the highest completed education proof are sent in paper, and only if the Embassy asks for them; everything else uploads to the portal
alerts: The deadline is a full year before enrolment: apply by 30 September 2026 for studies starting autumn 2027, so a missed round costs 12 months, not a semester

The announced window and the portal's call record differed slightly for this cycle (MEYS: from 21 August 2026; platform call: from 1 August 2026) - always submit as early as the platform allows rather than relying on the later date
The age window (born after 1 September 1991 and before 31 August 2008) is a hard filter on the platform and excludes older career changers

Students already enrolled at a Czech university must use the separate 'students already studying in the Czech Republic' call and additionally post a signed printed application to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs by 20 December 2026
Payment stops if you are outside the Czech Republic longer than 30 consecutive days, and only half is paid for a month with more than 15 days of absence for non-study reasons
The scholarship is not transferable: after the award you cannot change university, programme or the language of study, and taking longer than the standard two-year period ends the funding

The Faculty itself is not a contact point for this award - the Ministry's initial selection must be completed before the Faculty becomes involved, so questions go to registr@dzs.cz, not to FSV admissions
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill in the electronic application on the Study in Czechia portal section by section, take the English and general aptitude tests before 30 September, sit the Czech Embassy interview and hand over the certified documents on request, then wait for the Decision to arrive through the Embassy by the end of June and enrol at Charles University in autumn.
